questions.question:
Select the phrase/idiom that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

When our principal said she was leaving the company, I __played out the opportunity__ to fill the job.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"jumped at the opportunity"** is an idiomatic expression meaning to** eagerly seize a chance.**
 
• It correctly conveys the intended meaning of taking advantage quickly and enthusiastically.
 
• The other options **(glided, started, ran) **are not commonly used in this context and do not fit the idiomatic usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When our principal said she was leaving the company, I **jumped at the opportunity** to fill the job."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glided at the opportunity:** "Glided" implies a smooth movement and does not convey eagerness or seizing a chance.
 
• **Started at the opportunity:** "Started" can imply beginning something but does not fit idiomatically to mean eagerly taking a chance.
 
• **Ran to the opportunity:** "Ran" suggests physical movement towards something but is not idiomatic for seizing an opportunity.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.**

I have all the technical and communication skills necessary to crack any interview; it will be _______.

options.text: a storm in a tea cup
a piece of cake for me

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'a piece of cake for me'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank is: **a piece of cake for me.**
 
• Explanation: The idiom ***"a piece of cake"*** means something that is very easy to do or accomplish. In the context of the sentence, the speaker is confident in their technical and communication skills, believing that they can easily succeed in any interview. Therefore, **"a piece of cake for me" **accurately reflects the speaker's confidence in their abilities.
 
• **Options 1, 2, and 3 **do not convey the sense of ease or confidence implied by the sentence.
 
• Option 1, ***"a storm in a tea cup," ***describes a situation that is blown out of proportion, option 2,*** "a chip on my shoulder,***" refers to harboring resentment or a grudge, and option 3, ***"a hard nut to crack,"*** describes something that is difficult to achieve. Therefore, option 4,*** "a piece of cake for me,"*** is the most appropriate idiom in this context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Keep a straight face

options.text: Get on extremely well with someone
Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Keep a straight face:** This phrase refers to the act of maintaining a serious expression or not showing amusement in a situation where laughing or smiling might be the instinctive reaction. (बिना हँसे या अपना भाव बदले रखना)
 
• Correct Expression and Meaning: 'Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh' (बिना हँसे या अपना भाव बदले रहने का अर्थ है अपने चेहरे के भाव को नियंत्रित करना ताकि किसी मजाकिया स्थिति पर प्रतिक्रिया न दिखाई दे).
 
• **Example:** Despite the comic's hilarious jokes, she managed to **keep a straight face** throughout the performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Become very confused (बहुत भ्रमित होना): This suggests a state of perplexity or inability to understand something, which is not related to controlling one's facial expressions.
 
• Get on extremely well with someone (किसी के साथ बहुत अच्छे से मिलना-जुलना): This indicates a harmonious or very friendly relationship with another person, which again, has no connection to maintaining a neutral facial expression.
 
• Make more of an effort (अधिक प्रयास करना): This suggests trying harder in a general context, such as in work or personal endeavors, and does not specifically relate to the act of not showing laughter or amusement.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Crack someone up

options.text: To force someone to commit a mistake

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'To make someone laugh'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word meaning of the given idiom is **'To make someone laugh'.**
 
• Explanation: The idiom** "crack someone up" **means to make someone laugh uncontrollably or to cause amusement. It originated from the idea of causing someone to burst into laughter, often with the implication that the laughter is sudden and intense, like the sound of something cracking.
 
• ***For example,**__ if someone tells a hilarious joke that makes another person laugh so hard that they can't stop, you could say, "That joke really **cracked him up.**"*
 
• The origin of the **idiom** is not definitively known, but it likely stems from the concept of "**cracking**" **someone's composure or seriousness, replacing it with laughter. **

questions.question: The meaning of which of the following options is ‘Good luck’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom **"Break a leg"** is commonly used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.
 
• The expression originated from the theater, where wishing someone** "good luck"** was considered bad luck, so** "Break a leg"** was used instead.
 
• None of the other options convey a similar meaning of wishing good luck:
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Second banana" means a person who acts as a subordinate or backup.
 
• **Option 2:** "All wet" refers to being completely mistaken or wrong.
 
• **Option 3:** "Hang in there" means to persevere or keep going despite difficulties.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4: Break a leg**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I sent the agreement over for them to sign so __the ball is now in their court.__

options.text: An approach that uses traditional ideas that have previously worked
Better to be satisfied with what you have than risk losing it by trying to get something better
A time when after which programmes for older audiences may be aired on TV
It is time for someone to deal with a problem or make a decision, because other people have already done as much as they can

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"the ball is now in their court"** means that it is time for someone else to take action or make a decision because others have already done as much as they can. (अब बारी उनकी है)

 
 
• **Example: **We have made our final offer, and now** the ball is in their cour**t.
 
 
 
• **"It is time for someone to deal with a problem or make a decision, because other people have already done as much as they can"** indicates a shift in responsibility to another party. (अब निर्णय लेने का समय उनका है क्योंकि दूसरे लोग जितना कर सकते थे कर चुके हैं)
 
 
• **Example: **After months of negotiations, the proposal is complete, and now **the ball is in the management's court.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **An approach that uses traditional ideas that have previously worked** (ऐसा तरीका जो पहले काम कर चुका है):

 
 
• **Example: **She prefers an approach that uses traditional ideas that have previously worked in similar situations.
 
 
 
• **Better to be satisfied with what you have than risk losing it by trying to get something better** (जो है उससे संतुष्ट रहना बेहतर है बजाय इसके कि कुछ बेहतर पाने के लिए उसे खोने का जोखिम उठाया जाए):
 
 
• **Example: **He believes it's better to be satisfied with what you have than risk losing it by trying to get something better.
 
 
 
• **A time when after which programmes for older audiences may be aired on TV** (वह समय जिसके बाद टीवी पर वयस्क दर्शकों के लिए कार्यक्रम प्रसारित किए जा सकते हैं):
 
 
• **Example: **The watershed is the time when after which programmes for older audiences may be aired on TV.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

questions.question:
**Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence.**

He really ***stinks and smells foul*** after a hard session at the gym.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **pen and ink**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase "**stinks and smells foul**" refers to a very unpleasant smell (बहुत बुरी तरह से बदबू आना).

 
 
• **Example**: After jogging in the park during summer, he **stinks and smells foul**.
 
 
 
• The correct idiomatic expression "**pen and ink**" is used to imply something that smells bad (बदबू).
 
 
• **Example**: When he removed his shoes, the whole room was filled with **pen and ink**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is **pen and ink**.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **An old flame:** Refers to a former lover or someone with whom one had a romantic relationship (पुराना प्यार).

 
 
• **Example**: During the high school reunion, he was surprised to see his old flame.
 
 
 
• **An iron will**: Means having a very strong determination or willpower (मजबूत इच्छाशक्ति).
 
 
• **Example**: Despite the challenges, she completed her degree with an iron will.
 
 
 
• **Lame excuse**: A weak or poor excuse for something, not convincing (कमजोर बहाना).
 
 
• **Example**: He gave a lame excuse for his absence, saying his alarm clock didn't ring.
